key_highlights: ASX closed the week lower as traders positioned for higher RBA rates; mortgage and refinance rates rolling back across the board (39, 57)
Australian banks forecast the biggest house price falls on record, with housing construction expected to follow prices lower (58, 71)
Bathla's collapse flagged as a systemic warning for Australia's construction sector and broader 'Ponzi economy' fragility (53, 60)
EV sales outpaced petrol cars for the first time in Australia; BYD declares EV tipping point reached (20, 50, 56)
Iron ore market facing a structural shakeout masked by geopolitical conflict; materials sector under pressure (59)
ASIC launched a review of whistleblower complaints at major accounting firms, raising governance concerns (61)
Ratings agencies issued warnings on Victoria's soaring state debt (54)
Russia-Ukraine ceasefire and US-Canada $1.2T trade fallout reshaping global risk appetite (2, 13)
Small-cap ASX miners (Kaoko, Vanadium Resources, Piche, Brightstar, Solstice, Power Minerals) saw notable volume spikes (47, 49)
Aurum Resources added high-grade gold ounces in West Africa, supporting gold-explorer sentiment (48)

sectors.trend: Iron ore shakeout underway amid geopolitical distraction; gold explorers (Aurum) and small-cap miners (Kaoko, Vanadium, Piche, Brightstar, Solstice, Power Minerals) showing relative strength. Commodity demand softening.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin pressure from iron ore price weakness. Gold and critical-mines names (AUR.AX, VDL.AX, PCH.AX) offer diversification. Monitor iron ore contract pricing vs. spot.

sectors.trend: Banks forecasting record house price declines; CBA and Westpac facing scrutiny over pricing loopholes for loyal customers. ASIC whistleblower review at Big Four accounting firms adds governance overhang. Higher rate expectations pressure equity valuations.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, WBC.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX may see NIM support from higher rates but credit-loss provisions will rise with housing downturn. Regulatory risk elevated. REITs (VGP.AX, SGP.AX) face rising financing costs.

sectors.trend: EV sales surpassed petrol cars for the first time in Australia; BYD confirms tipping point. BW LPG benefiting from strait dynamics. Fuel cost spikes accelerating consumer shift.
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WES.AX face structural volume risk from EV adoption. BWL.AX benefits from LNG logistics. Battery and charging-infrastructure names gain. Oil majors (WDS.AX) under longer-term pressure.

sectors.trend: Bathla collapse signals sector-wide fragility; housing construction to follow falling prices. Brisbane waterfront approval (2,200 homes, zero affordable) highlights affordability crisis. Victoria debt warnings add sovereign-credit risk.
sectors.implications: CGP.AX, WBC.AX (mortgage book), and property developers face elevated default risk. REITs under pressure from higher rates and falling occupier demand. State-guaranteed bonds (VIC) under scrutiny.

sectors.trend: Vietnam dental tourism expansion threatens Australian dental practitioners. Cigarette tax political fight intensifies. Qantas engine-fire incident raises safety/insurance costs for aviation.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX, WES.AX (health segment) relatively insulated. QAN.AX faces operational and reputational risk. Tobacco-linked consumer names face regulatory headwinds.

sectors.trend: AI chip demand strong (Monolithic Power +48% revenue); drone disruption in defence; Australia faces AI-worker and skilled-labour shortages. Robo.ai revenue up but balance sheet fragile.
sectors.implications: ASX-listed tech/defence names (e.g., CNA.AX, WES.AX tech segment) benefit from AI capex cycle. Skilled-migration policy (Pocock) supports labour supply. Monitor ASIC governance actions.

key_themes: RBA rate path: market bracing for higher-for-longer; mortgage rates rolling back (39, 57)
Housing correction: banks forecast record price falls; construction to follow (58, 71)
Construction sector fragility: Bathla collapse as systemic warning (53, 60)
EV inflection point: petrol cars overtaken; structural shift underway (20, 50, 56)
Iron ore structural shakeout masked by war (59)
Geopolitical: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire, US-Canada trade rupture (2, 13)
Regulatory scrutiny: ASIC whistleblower review, bank pricing loopholes (61, 67)
Labour shortages: AI workers, tradies; migration policy debate (46, 14, 26)
Small-cap mining momentum: gold and critical-mines explorers active (47, 48, 49)

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Housing market correction and credit losses
risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce exposure to property-linked REITs and construction names; favour banks with strong provision buffers (CBA.AX, NAB.AX). Monitor NIM vs. credit-cost spread.
Hedge duration risk; favour short-duration and dividend-yielding equities. Monitor 10-yr GBA yield and AUD/USD.
Diversify materials exposure toward gold (AUR.AX) and critical minerals; reduce single-commodity concentration in BHP.AX/RIO.AX.
Maintain 10-15% cash/defensive allocation; monitor commodity supply-chain disruptions.
Avoid high-leverage property developers; favour established builders with government contract backlogs.
Monitor ASIC enforcement actions; favour banks with clean governance records.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Climate events (El Niño cyclones, Qld bushfires)
risk_assessment.mitigation: Review insurance coverage on physical assets; monitor energy and infrastructure exposure.

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold and critical-mines explorers as iron ore weakens
opportunities.rationale: Iron ore shakeout (59) pressures BHP/RIO/FMG; gold (Aurum) and vanadium/power-minerals names offer relative strength and inflation hedge.
EV sales surpassed petrol cars; BYD confirms tipping point. Charging infrastructure, battery, and grid-upgrade names gain structurally.

opportunities.recommendation: Favour quality banks with strong provision buffers
opportunities.rationale: Higher rates support NIM; CBA and NAB have stronger capital positions ahead of housing credit losses.
Strait dynamics and LNG logistics tailwind; energy transition supports long-term demand.

defensive_moves.rationale: Record house price falls forecast; Bathla collapse signals sector contagion risk; construction to follow prices lower.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge rate risk with short-duration and dividend-yielding equities
defensive_moves.rationale: Market bracing for higher RBA rates; mortgage rates rolling back pressures rate-sensitive sectors.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain 10-15% cash/defensive allocation for geopolitical volatility
defensive_moves.rationale: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire fragile; US-Canada $1.2T trade fallout; El Niño climate risks.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Monitor ASIC and bank-pricing regulatory developments
defensive_moves.rationale: Whistleblower review at Big Four and bank pricing loopholes could trigger enforcement actions affecting financials.

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain under pressure over the next 1-3 months as RBA rate expectations firm, housing data deteriorates, and iron ore weakness feeds through to materials earnings. Defensive rotation into utilities, healthcare (CSL.AX), and quality banks (CBA.AX, NAB.AX) expected. Small-cap miners may see continued speculative activity. Key watch: RBA statement, CPI print, and housing-approval data.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautiously constructive if the 'bull case' (62) materialises via rate cuts in H2 2026. EV transition, AI capex, and critical-mines demand support structural growth. However, housing correction depth and construction-sector fragility (60) could delay recovery. Canada outperforming Australia on per-capita GDP (64) underscores productivity concerns. Gold and energy remain key hedges.

XRP / BTC price action as risk-appetite proxy
